title: Ferman Tapp's band
summary: Thomas names Sam Utterback and Svetti as members of the good band, which broadcast and played three shows a night, and says arrangements may have been Charlie Dixon's.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: I heard about that. Did Ferman Tapp have a good band?
JT (2 of 1) 99
I thought it was a good band.
Well, I mean who else was in that, Joe?
Les, I can't remember Les' last name but there was a trumpet player and he played the English horn by the name of Sam Utterback.
Sam?
Utterback.
How do you spell that?
Utterback, U-t-t-e-r-b-a-c-k.
I never heard of him before.
Yeah, well, he could play. And another fellow by the name of Svetti (?), he played trumpet. And Les? It was a good band. ...
Well, I never heard of Ferman Tapp until Dicky Wells told me he worked for Ferman Tapp back in Louisville in a roadhouse.
Well, Dicky is much older than I am. Dicky Wells, he's a trombonist.
Leave it on. But, Ferman Tapp, how come he got to be a leader?
Who knows. I don't know.
But, did he have, was he a good musician?
Yes, he was.
Oh, he was? That's interesting.
We doin' a broadcasting thing and three shows a night and all those kinds of things.
Yeah. Oh, well, he must have been.
Oh, he's a good musician.
Well, who would do his arrangements?

I don't know. I really don't know. It might have been, it could have been Charlie Dixon. It could have been because some of those things had the touch that Charlie Dixon had and Dixon had the idea of arranging ...
